title: SMTO-SKL-0081 — That file or folder name isn't allowed in OneDrive or SharePoint

headings.title: SMTO-SKL-0081 — That file or folder name isn't allowed in OneDrive or SharePoint

html:
SMTO-SKL-0081 — That file or folder name isn't allowed in OneDrive or SharePoint

GUID: 19357def-ca69-5ed3-80c3-acde80687492
Slug: microsoft365-invalid-filename
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • The name SMTO was going to give a file or folder isn't allowed in OneDrive or SharePoint. SMTO stopped before sending anything, so nothing was created or changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Choose a name without any of these characters: / \ : * ? " < > |, and without a dot or space at the end, for example “Report November 2026.pdf”. OneDrive and SharePoint don't allow those characters in names.
  2. To put it inside a folder, tell SMTO the folder separately instead of writing the folder into the name. A slash in the name looks like a folder path, which isn't allowed in a single name.
  3. Ask SMTO to do the upload, copy, move or new folder again with the new name. Nothing was created the first time, so repeating it won't make a duplicate.

What success looks like

  • The file or folder appears in OneDrive or SharePoint with the name you chose.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the name you tried, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't put a folder path inside the name; tell SMTO the folder separately.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Microsoft 365 upload_name rejected the requested file or folder name: it was empty, longer than 255 characters, '.' or '..', contained / \ : * ? " < > | or a line break, or ended with a dot or space.

What this means

  • Upload filename is empty, too long, a dot path, contains forbidden separators/punctuation/control characters or ends in a dot/space. This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Upload filename is empty, too long, a dot path, contains forbidden separators/punctuation/control characters or ends in a dot/space.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the leaf name independently of its source artifact path.

How to fix it

  • Supply a non-empty leaf name of at most 255 characters with no path separators, none of : * ? " < > |, no line breaks, not '.' or '..', and not ending in a dot or space; then repeat file_upload, folder_create, file_move or file_copy with that name. Use parent_item_id for the folder location instead of a path in the name.
  • Use a nonempty leaf filename without path separators, reserved punctuation, trailing dots or spaces.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended filename satisfies all upload-name constraints.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.
